geometry.derivationNote: Treat the 1813 signature as the legal-basis event only. Presidential Library chronology states full Persian recognition/entry into force in 1818; exact 1818 effective date must be resolved before geometry-verified replay.
The 1828 Military Topographic Depot map explicitly depicts the new boundary. It is a geometry-verification candidate, but must be georeferenced and checked against treaty clauses before promotion.
Georeference the Danube-mouth islands, Black Sea coastal line and Akhalkalaki/Akhaltsikhe districts from the treaty and period official maps; do not substitute modern administrative borders.

effectiveDate.note: Articles I and IV make the cession and right of immediate possession complete and absolute upon exchange of ratifications. The later 18 October ceremony at Sitka is retained as a separate physical/formal-transfer event and does not drive the russian-legal-border replay.

geometry.derivationNote: The treaty itself defines the ceded Russian possessions and reproduces the 1825 eastern boundary, including the 141st meridian sector. Do not promote a full cession polygon until the southeastern panhandle, islands, western Bering limit and historical coastlines are reconstructed from the treaty and authoritative cartography. The legal effective date is now verified independently of that remaining geometry work.

territoryChanges.notes: Legacy change id retained for compatibility; semantically this change now represents legal cession on 20 June 1867, not the 18 October formal delivery ceremony.
